critical_files.note: 8 endpoints, 2 missing text guards (rsCompare/rsDeAI), unbounded fields, import style
core new module — Windows case bug, symlink gap, contract inconsistency, SRP

SEC-001_reassessment.root_cause: resolveWorkspaceRootForRequest (services/workflow.ts:206 + workflow-revision.ts:38) returns caller-supplied workspace.identity.workspaceRoot verbatim when existsSync passes, bypassing safeResolveWorkspaceRoot containment.
SEC-001_reassessment.verification: Deep-dive traced the full attack path. workspace.identity.workspaceRoot IS attacker-controllable (workspace-model.ts:323 reads identityRecord.workspaceRoot from request body). HOWEVER all endpoint callers (workflowRoute/workflowPlan/workflowRevisionStartSession and 13 sibling endpoints) route through resolveWorkspace(body) (endpoints/workflow.ts:47-59) which OVERRIDES identity.workspaceRoot with the safe resolveWorkspaceRoot()→safeResolveWorkspaceRoot() value before passing to the service. Therefore resolveWorkspaceRootForRequest sees the already-contained root, not the attacker value. No live bypass via any current endpoint. Confirmed no non-endpoint callers (only endpoints/workflow.ts + tests).
SEC-001_reassessment.risk_if_unfixed: Defense-in-depth gap: the service function trusts its input. A future caller that passes raw request workspace without the resolveWorkspace override would bypass containment. The phase's containment is enforced at the endpoint layer, not the service boundary — fragile for a security primitive.
SEC-001_reassessment.remediation: Either (a) apply safeResolveWorkspaceRoot containment to the requested path inside resolveWorkspaceRootForRequest before returning, or (b) document the contract that callers MUST sanitize and add an assertion. Option (a) is preferred for defense-in-depth.

SEC-002_verification.verification: Confirmed via grep + code read: reader-endpoints.ts has 8 validateStringLength calls (lines 382,408,550,623,665,670,760,763) across rsAnalyze/rsCreateCustomPersona/rsGetOverlay/rsAIFlavor/rsFeedback. rsCompareEndpoint (line 918) and rsDeAIEndpoint (line 1034) have ZERO validateStringLength calls. textA/textB (rsCompare) and text (rsDeAI) only get typeof checks. TASK-002 summary INACCURATELY claimed these endpoints were guarded. Real DoS gap.

SEC-003_verification.verification: Confirmed: rsDeAIEndpoint (line 1034) reads body.text, checks only typeof, passes unbounded text to detectAIFlavor + revisionService.revise. No validateStringLength. novelId also unbounded in this endpoint.

CORR-001_verification.verification: Confirmed: input-validation.ts:91-98 uses path.normalize (does NOT change case) + string startsWith. Comment at line 90 claims 'On Windows, normalize both paths for case-insensitive comparison' but path.normalize does not lowercase. On Windows (case-insensitive NTFS), if NIKO_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE case differs from process.cwd() case, containment check throws false-positive. Misleading comment + real correctness bug on the dev platform.

findings.title: rsCompareEndpoint textA/textB lack length guard — SEC-001 DoS fix incomplete
findings.description: rsCompareEndpoint validates textA/textB are non-empty strings but never calls validateStringLength. Both texts flow unbounded into DualEngine.analyze (run concurrently, doubling impact). TASK-002 summary inaccurately claimed this endpoint was guarded.
findings.impact: Attacker can POST two arbitrarily large text bodies to /reader/compare, bypassing the 100k-char guard enforced on rsAnalyze/rsAIFlavor. Directly reintroduces SEC-001 DoS on this endpoint.
findings.suggestion: Add validateStringLength(textA, MAX_TEXT_LENGTH, 'versionA.text') and same for textB before engine.analyze. Also bound novelId (MAX_NOVEL_ID_LENGTH) which is also unguarded here.

findings.title: rsDeAIEndpoint text + novelId lack length guard — SEC-001 DoS fix incomplete
findings.description: rsDeAIEndpoint checks novelId/text are strings but adds no validateStringLength. Unbounded text flows into detectAIFlavor and revisionService.revise (runs revision iterations).
findings.impact: Multi-MB text to /reader/de-ai bypasses the 100k guard; amplified by revision iterations. Reintroduces SEC-001.
findings.suggestion: Add validateStringLength(novelId, MAX_NOVEL_ID_LENGTH, 'novelId') and validateStringLength(text, MAX_TEXT_LENGTH, 'text') after the typeof checks.

findings.title: Windows case-sensitivity false-positive in safeResolveWorkspaceRoot containment
findings.description: Containment uses path.normalize + string startsWith. path.normalize does not lowercase. On Windows (case-insensitive NTFS), if NIKO_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE case differs from process.cwd() case, the check throws a false-positive 'path traversal'. Comment at line 90 falsely claims case-insensitive comparison is performed.
findings.impact: Legitimate workspace paths are rejected on Windows (the dev platform) when env case differs from cwd case — all 12 endpoint/service callers throw → endpoints return 500. Availability + correctness bug in the core new security module.
findings.suggestion: Use path.relative(root, resolved) and reject if result starts with '..' or is absolute (platform-agnostic, case-tolerant on Windows via path.relative semantics), OR lowercase both sides on Windows (process.platform === 'win32'). Fix the misleading comment either way.

findings.title: input-validation.ts placement in mcp/ causes services→mcp layering + couples workspace resolution with HTTP transport
findings.description: Module lives at src-ts/mcp/ and imports HttpResponse/jsonResponse from ./http-types.js. Consequently src-ts/services/revision-service.ts imports from ../mcp/input-validation.js — the FIRST services→mcp dependency edge (verified: no other services/ file imports mcp/). safeResolveWorkspaceRoot is transport-agnostic path/env logic but is structurally coupled to HTTP types, forcing any non-HTTP consumer to pull in transport types.
findings.impact: Layering precedent: future services→mcp edges become acceptable. A CLI or alternate transport needing safe workspace resolution must import HTTP response types. Reader domain constants (MAX_NOVEL_ID_LENGTH etc.) also live in the MCP layer despite being Reader-domain.
findings.suggestion: Split: move safeResolveWorkspaceRoot + workspace env handling to src-ts/utils/workspace.ts (transport-neutral). Keep validateStringLength/validateWeight + their HTTP-returning contract in mcp/input-validation.ts (or move all to utils/ if HttpResponse import is decoupled). Reader domain constants belong in src-ts/reader/.

findings.title: resolveWorkspaceRootForRequest trusts caller-supplied workspaceRoot without containment (defense-in-depth gap)
findings.description: Service function returns workspace.identity.workspaceRoot verbatim when existsSync passes, bypassing safeResolveWorkspaceRoot. Deep-dive confirmed NO live bypass: all endpoint callers sanitize via resolveWorkspace(body) which overrides identity.workspaceRoot with the safe root. But the service contract is unsafe — it trusts input.
findings.impact: Latent: a future caller passing raw request workspace (without the resolveWorkspace override) would bypass containment. Containment is enforced at the endpoint layer, not the service boundary — fragile for a security primitive.
findings.suggestion: Apply containment inside resolveWorkspaceRootForRequest: resolve the requested path and verify it is within safeResolveWorkspaceRoot() before returning; else fall back to safe root. Defense-in-depth at the service boundary.

findings.title: rsFeedbackEndpoint personaId/dimension unbounded — map-key DoS
findings.description: novelId and feedbackId get validateStringLength; personaId and dimension only get typeof checks. Both are used as Map keys (feedbackAggregateStore, inner dimension Map) with no length cap or cardinality bound.
findings.impact: Unbounded string keys grow memory; high-cardinality dimension values grow the store unboundedly. DoS via memory exhaustion.
findings.suggestion: Bound personaId (MAX_NOVEL_ID_LENGTH) and dimension (MAX_NAME_LENGTH) with validateStringLength after the type checks.

findings.title: focusAreas[]/biases[] arrays unbounded in createCustomPersona — unbounded storage
findings.description: Arrays validated as arrays but no cap on array length or per-element string length. Persisted to reader-personas.json and held in customPersonaStore.
findings.impact: Attacker creates personas with huge arrays/long elements → unbounded in-memory store + inflated persisted file + amplified writes on every save.
findings.suggestion: Cap array length (e.g. <=64) and per-element length (validateStringLength) before accepting.

findings.title: rsDeAIEndpoint targetStyle unbounded — flows into RevisionService quality goals
findings.description: targetStyle read with no length validation, interpolated into qualityGoals and passed as target_style to revisionService.revise.
findings.impact: Arbitrarily long targetStyle bloats revision payload/prompt size. Inconsistency in SEC-001 rollout.
findings.suggestion: validateStringLength(targetStyle, MAX_NAME_LENGTH, 'targetStyle') when mode==='style-shift'.

findings.title: safeResolveWorkspaceRoot does not resolve symlinks — containment bypass via symlink/junction
findings.description: path.resolve/normalize do not resolve symlinks, junctions, or Windows substituted drives. If allowed root contains a symlink pointing outside, a path naming that symlink's subtree passes lexical containment but resolves outside at I/O time.
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth gap; exploitability requires a symlink planted inside cwd (not a direct remote attack).
findings.suggestion: Use fs.realpathSync on both resolved and root before comparison (catch ENOENT → fail safe). Acceptable to defer if threat model is remote-env-only, but document the assumption.

findings.title: Path traversal throw propagates as 500 with internal path leak
findings.description: safeResolveWorkspaceRoot throws 'Workspace path traversal detected: "<resolved>" is outside allowed root "<root>"'. Callers (chat/critic/workspace/graph/memory/wiki/workflow/agent) call it without a local try/catch; the throw propagates to the outer handler catch → 500 with the error message in the body.
findings.impact: (1) Security rejection mis-classified as 500 (should be 400/403). (2) Internal absolute paths (resolved + root) echoed to the caller — information disclosure of host filesystem layout.
findings.suggestion: Wrap callers in a helper that catches the traversal Error and returns 400/403 with a generic message ('Invalid workspace configuration'), logging the detail server-side only.

findings.title: NIKO_WORKSPACE_ALLOW_OUTSIDE escape hatch silently downgrades containment with no audit signal
findings.description: Escape hatch disables containment when env === 'true'. No startup warning log, no production guard, no observability. ~20 test files set this var; if CI/test env leaks into a production build, containment silently reverts with no operator signal.
findings.impact: Misconfigured deployment silently reverts SEC-002. Defense-in-depth + operational-safety gap.
findings.suggestion: Emit a startup warning log when ALLOW_OUTSIDE is enabled. Consider restricting to non-production (NODE_ENV guard) or requiring an explicit path allowlist.

findings.title: safeResolveWorkspaceRoot behavior change for relative/env-outside paths
findings.description: Old impl returned trim(env)||cwd verbatim (relative env stayed relative). New impl force-resolves (path.resolve) and adds containment. Relative env now becomes absolute; env pointing outside cwd now throws (unless ALLOW_OUTSIDE).
findings.impact: Deployments relying on relative env or cwd-external legit workspace break on upgrade. Behavior change not in CHANGELOG.
findings.suggestion: Document the behavior change in CHANGELOG; document NIKO_WORKSPACE_ALLOW_OUTSIDE for legitimate cwd-external workspaces.

findings.title: chat.ts length-overflow status code inconsistency (413 for per-message, 400 for total chars)
findings.description: Refactor changed per-message overflow 400→413 (via validateStringLength) but MAX_TOTAL_CHARS overflow still returns 400. Same endpoint returns two different codes for length overflow. 413 (Payload Too Large) is conventionally for whole-payload size; field validation is usually 400/422. No 413 precedent elsewhere in src-ts/mcp/.
findings.impact: Downstream clients branching on 400 mis-classify per-message overflow; inconsistent codes within one endpoint.
findings.suggestion: Unify: either 413 for both length overflows or 400/422 for both. If keeping 413, document the decision and apply uniformly.

findings.title: personaIds array elements unbounded — DoS via long persona IDs
findings.description: personaIds loop validates each element is a string but applies no length cap. {personaIds:['x'.repeat(1e7)]} passes type check, flows into resolvePersonas + logging of the whole array.
findings.impact: Long persona IDs amplify memory + log volume, bypassing SEC-001.
findings.suggestion: validateStringLength(id, MAX_NOVEL_ID_LENGTH, 'personaId') inside the loop (rsAnalyze line 390 and rsCompare line 954).

findings.title: Reader domain constants live in MCP transport layer
findings.description: MAX_NOVEL_ID_LENGTH/MAX_TEXT_LENGTH/MAX_NAME_LENGTH are Reader-domain boundaries but live in src-ts/mcp/. Only reader-endpoints.ts + tests use them. Forces Reader to import from mcp/.
findings.impact: Reader domain boundaries structurally in MCP layer; future Reader components must depend on mcp/.
findings.suggestion: Move to src-ts/reader/constants.ts; input-validation.ts keeps only transport-level limits (e.g. MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS) if any.

findings.title: Inconsistent validator contract — 2 return HttpResponse|null, 1 throws
findings.description: validateStringLength/validateWeight return HttpResponse|null (guard-return). safeResolveWorkspaceRoot returns string OR throws. Three 'validators' documented as one pattern have three error contracts. Callers cannot uniformly `if(err) return err`.
findings.impact: Maintainers can't infer the error path from the name; throw can surface as unhandled 500 (see REV-010).
findings.suggestion: Unify: make safeResolveWorkspaceRoot return {ok, value}|{error: HttpResponse} OR rename to a distinct 'resolver' category and document the throw contract explicitly.

findings.title: Local resolveWorkspaceRoot() wrappers are needless indirection
findings.description: 7 endpoint files + reader keep a local resolveWorkspaceRoot()/getWorkspaceRoot() whose body is now `return safeResolveWorkspaceRoot()` — a zero-value pass-through. For non-exported wrappers (most endpoints) there's no compat benefit.
findings.impact: Extra stack frame + two places to maintain for behavior changes. 'Single source of truth' not fully realized — entry points still re-wrapped per file.
findings.suggestion: Inline safeResolveWorkspaceRoot at call sites and drop the non-exported wrappers. Keep named wrappers only where they're a deliberate seam (chat/workflow resolveWorkflowWorkspace).

findings.title: Single-responsibility: path resolution mixed with input validation
findings.description: Module bundles SEC-001 (length), SEC-002 (path/env resolution), SEC-004 (weight). safeResolveWorkspaceRoot resolves process env config + containment — not request-input validation. Different concern from the two payload validators.
findings.impact: Low cohesion: workspace-only consumers transitively pull HTTP types + length/weight validators.
findings.suggestion: Split into utils/workspace.ts (resolver) + mcp/input-validation.ts (payload validators). See REV-004.

findings.title: reader-endpoints.ts:28 import violates Prettier printWidth (166 chars > 100) and bundles 6 symbols
findings.description: Single-line import bundles 6 named imports (3 functions + 3 constants) — 166 chars, exceeding Prettier printWidth 100. All other multi-imports in the file are wrapped one-per-line with trailing comma. Prettier --write would auto-reformat → churn.
findings.impact: Inconsistent with project formatting; fails format:check if touched; horizontal scroll.
findings.suggestion: Wrap one-name-per-line with trailing comma to match surrounding convention.

findings.title: Inconsistent ESM specifier — new import adds .js suffix while surrounding imports omit it
findings.description: Lines 10-27 omit .js suffix (codebase relies on scripts/postprocess_esm_imports.cjs to append at build). Line 28 adds .js manually. Postprocessor idempotently skips already-suffixed specifiers, so functionally fine, but mixed style within one import block.
findings.impact: Readers wonder why one import carries the suffix; minor inconsistency.
findings.suggestion: Match file convention (drop .js) or make it a coordinated codebase-wide change — don't mix within a file.

findings.title: safeResolveWorkspaceRoot name vague — 'safe' from what?
findings.description: 'safe' is a vague modifier; name doesn't convey path-traversal/containment. JSDoc says 'Safely resolve' similarly vague. A reader might misread as 'no-throw' while it throws on traversal.
findings.impact: New readers must read full JSDoc to grasp security semantics; potential misread.
findings.suggestion: Consider resolveContainedWorkspaceRoot (conveys containment). If not renaming, replace 'Safely' with 'Containment-guarded' in JSDoc.

findings.title: Magic numbers 256/200 lack rationale; novel/story terminology mixed
findings.description: MAX_TEXT_LENGTH documents the 100k-vs-24k-chat relationship, but MAX_NOVEL_ID_LENGTH=256 and MAX_NAME_LENGTH=200 have only a one-line 'Maximum length for...' comment. 'novel/story identifiers' mixes two domain terms.
findings.impact: Future threshold tuners don't know the safety margin; terminology drift risk.
findings.suggestion: Add rationale per constant (e.g. '256 — accommodates UUID/slug with headroom'); unify terminology to 'novel identifier'.

findings.title: safeResolveWorkspaceRoot tests missing Windows separator + case boundary
findings.description: Tests use 'C:/Windows/System32' (forward slash) for Windows absolute path. Missing: backslash form, case-mismatch boundary (NTFS case-insensitive — relates to REV-003). The code comment claims case-insensitive handling that the tests don't exercise.
findings.impact: Windows case bug (REV-003) has no test coverage; misleading comment unguarded.
findings.suggestion: Add backslash + case-mismatch test cases reflecting whichever behavior is adopted (case-normalized or documented-as-absent).

findings.title: Escape-hatch test coverage insufficient — non-'true' ALLOW_OUTSIDE values untested
findings.description: Only ALLOW_OUTSIDE='true' is tested. The strict === 'true' comparison means '1'/'TRUE'/'' do NOT enable the hatch — a conservative design, but untested. Future loosening to truthy would silently weaken the security contract.
findings.impact: Security-relevant branch has no regression guard.
findings.suggestion: Add a test asserting non-'true' values ('1','TRUE','') do NOT allow outside.

findings.title: Test title contradicts its assertion
findings.description: it('returns 413 for empty string when limit is 0') asserts expect(result).toBeNull() (i.e. does NOT return 413). Title is the inverse of the behavior.
findings.impact: Test intent misread; future regressions misdiagnosed.
findings.suggestion: Rename to 'returns null for empty string at limit 0 (boundary)' or delete (line 42 covers length===limit).

findings.title: validateWeight error message ambiguous for non-number types
findings.description: 'must be a finite number, got ${value}' — for an object, renders 'got [object Object]'; for a string '0.5', indistinguishable from a numeric out-of-range.
findings.impact: Client can't distinguish type error vs range error.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish non-number branch: 'must be a number, got ${typeof value}' or truncate.

findings.title: adjustPersonaWeights NaN fallback to 0.5 is undocumented + silent
findings.description: Non-finite weight silently falls back to 0.5 (magic default, no comment, no log). Safer than old (NaN propagated) but hides corrupted store data.
findings.impact: Corrupted persona weights silently reset on feedback adjust; hard to trace.
findings.suggestion: Log _log.warn when falling back, or extract DEFAULT_WEIGHT=0.5 constant with comment.

findings.title: critic.ts chapters[]/chapterMeta[] unbounded
findings.description: runConsistencyCheck accepts chapters array with no length or per-string cap; feeds analysis engines. Pre-existing gap surfaced by the completeness sweep.
findings.impact: Huge chapters array inflates analysis cost; lower severity (less-exposed endpoint).
findings.suggestion: Cap array length + per-string length consistent with MAX_TEXT_LENGTH patterns.

findings.title: validateWeight error echoes raw value — potential reflection
findings.description: Error interpolates `got ${value}` for unknown input. Current callers pre-guard with typeof, so strings don't reach it — but the shared helper could echo a large payload if reused without the guard.
findings.impact: Minimal now; latent if reused unguarded.
findings.suggestion: Truncate reflected value to ~64 chars.

findings.title: safeResolveWorkspaceRoot recomputes path.normalize(root) per call — root is invariant
findings.description: Called once per request from 8+ endpoints; root (cwd/arg) is invariant per process but normalized every call.
findings.impact: Negligible — sub-microsecond on short paths, not a hot loop. No measurable degradation.
findings.suggestion: Optional micro-memo keyed by root. Do NOT memo on env alone (runtime-mutable). Low priority.

findings.title: path.resolve already normalizes — explicit path.normalize on resolved is redundant
findings.description: path.resolve yields canonical absolute path; path.normalize on its output is a no-op on POSIX, collapses redundant separators on Windows.
findings.impact: Negligible.
findings.suggestion: Optional cleanup: drop explicit normalize on resolved (keep on root if root can arrive non-normalized).

findings.title: rsAnalyzeEndpoint if(manuscriptText) guard intent unclear
findings.description: if(manuscriptText) skips length check for empty; adjacent line 413 short-circuits empty text. Two adjacent empty-checks with different intent.
findings.impact: Reader pause; minor.
findings.suggestion: Comment 'Skip length check for empty text — handled below' or merge into linear flow.

findings.title: rsAIFlavor vs rsAnalyze text guard style inconsistency
findings.description: rsAIFlavor uses 'text !== undefined && typeof string'; rsAnalyze uses 'if(manuscriptText)' (truthy). rsAIFlavor calls validateStringLength on '' (harmless but redundant); rsAnalyze skips ''.
findings.impact: Cognitive overhead switching endpoints.
findings.suggestion: Unify guard style (truthy 'if(text)') or extract validateOptionalText helper.

findings.title: Inconsistent workspace-resolution wrapping — critic inlines, others wrap, reader wraps trivially
findings.description: critic.ts inlines safeResolveWorkspaceRoot(); 7 endpoints wrap in resolveWorkspaceRoot(); reader's getWorkspaceRoot is a zero-value pass-through. Three styles for one operation.
findings.impact: If a workspace hook is added later, critic + reader need separate edits; easy to miss.
findings.suggestion: Pick one style project-wide (wrap everywhere or inline everywhere).

findings.title: getPersonasFilePath uses require('node:path') instead of top-level import (pre-existing)
findings.description: require('node:path') for join while fs uses dynamic import. ESM anti-pattern; input-validation.ts now uses top-level import path, amplifying the inconsistency.
findings.impact: Style inconsistency; require behavior can differ from import in some resolvers.
findings.suggestion: Top-level import path from 'node:path'; use path.join. Pre-existing but worsened by contrast.

findings.title: beforeEach/afterEach env save/restore could be a shared helper
findings.description: ~20 lines of env save/restore boilerplate. Other env-dependent tests likely repeat it.
findings.impact: Minor duplication; single use today.
findings.suggestion: Extract saveRestoreEnv(keys) helper when a second use appears (YAGNI for now).

findings.title: exported-constants tests assert hardcoded literals (no protection value)
findings.description: Three tests assert MAX_*=256/100000/200 — callers use the symbol not the literal, and tsc catches undefined refs. Tests are 'expect(256).toBe(256)'.
findings.impact: Maintenance burden (change constant → change test) with no real regression guard; false coverage signal.
findings.suggestion: Delete, or assert semantic relations (MAX_TEXT_LENGTH > MAX_NOVEL_ID_LENGTH).

findings.title: validateWeight JSDoc says inclusive but error says 'between' (implies exclusive)
findings.description: JSDoc: 'inclusive'. Error: 'must be between min and max' — 'between' in English often implies exclusive. Tests confirm 0/1 pass (inclusive).
findings.impact: Client may misinfer boundary rejection.
findings.suggestion: Error: 'must be in [min, max] (inclusive)' or 'must be between min and max inclusive'.

findings.title: NIKO_WORKSPACE_ALLOW_OUTSIDE not registered in a config layer
findings.description: New process-level env var read via process.env magic string; no central registry (src-ts/config/, mcp/config.ts).
findings.impact: Operators/security reviewers must scan source to discover security-bypass flags.
findings.suggestion: Register alongside NIKO_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE in a config module with default + docs.

findings.title: Redundant typeof guard before Number.isFinite
findings.description: Number.isFinite already rejects non-numbers; typeof check is redundant. Defensible as belt-and-suspenders for the unknown contract.
findings.impact: None functionally.
findings.suggestion: Keep with a one-line comment, or simplify to !Number.isFinite(value).

findings.title: Tests repeat result!.statusCode + result!.body as {error:string} boilerplate
findings.description: 8+ tests repeat the non-null assertion + inline cast.
findings.impact: Minor repetition; safe (preceded by not.toBeNull).
findings.suggestion: Optional getErrorBody(result) helper. Low priority.

findings.title: validateStringLength takes string (not unknown) — asymmetric with validateWeight; two import lines from http-types
findings.description: validateWeight defensively types unknown; validateStringLength assumes string. Current callers pre-guard with typeof, so safe. Also: two separate import lines from ./http-types.js (type + value) — matches dominant mcp/endpoints convention, not a defect.
findings.impact: API asymmetry; a future caller forgetting the typeof guard would throw on .length instead of clean 413.
findings.suggestion: Either accept unknown + internal typeof→400, or document the precondition. Import style: no change (matches convention).

spec_compliance.note: Convergence criteria from TASK files were mechanically met (grep counts pass) but COVERAGE claims in TASK-002 summary were inaccurate — rsCompare/rsDeAI endpoints claimed guarded but are not. Spec-compliance re-check flags this as a substantive gap, not a grep-count gap.

convergence_grep_results.validateStringLength_in_reader_endpoints: 8 matches (criteria required >=7) — PASS mechanically, but 2 endpoints (rsCompare, rsDeAI) have ZERO guards despite summary claiming coverage

next_step: WARN verdict: proceed to /quality-test with caveats, but recommend a lightweight fix loop for the 3 security-completeness HIGHs (REV-001/002/003) first — they are in the phase's own scope and are trivial fixes (add validateStringLength to 2 endpoints; Windows case normalization). REV-004 (module placement) is architectural and can be deferred.
